proof.text: *Setup.* For $U\in\mathsf{FEt}(Y)$ with structure map $p:U\to Y$, the base change $U_0=U\times_YY_0$ is finite etale over $Y_0$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], and by pasting the cartesian squares $U_0\to Y_0\to S_0$ over $U\to Y\to S$ [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] $U_0=U\times_SS_0$ is also the closed fibre of $U$ over $S$. Since $p$ is finite and $f$ is proper, $f\circ p:U\to S$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](c). So every $U\in\mathsf{FEt}(Y)$, and every scheme finite over such a $U$, is a proper $S$-scheme whose closed fibre is its base change to $Y_0$.

source.place: ## Proof, first sentences (properness of Z over S)

proof.text: *Morphisms are sections.* Let $U,V\in\mathsf{FEt}(Y)$ and $P=V\times_YU$ with second projection $\pi:P\to U$, which is finite etale (base change of $V\to Y$, [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]). By the universal property of the fibre product, $\varphi\mapsto s_\varphi=(\varphi,\mathrm{id}_U)$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(U,V)$ to the set of sections of $\pi$ (inverse: $s\mapsto\mathrm{pr}_1\circ s$). Base change to $Y_0$ gives $P_0=P\times_YY_0=V_0\times_{Y_0}U_0$ with $\pi_0:P_0\to U_0$, and $(s_\varphi)_0=s_{\varphi_0}$, so this bijection commutes with $\varphi\mapsto\varphi_0$ and $s\mapsto s_0$.

*Sections are clopen pieces of degree one.* $\pi$ is finite, hence separated, and etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion] a section $s$ of $\pi$ is an open and closed immersion, $W_s=s(U)$ is an open and closed subscheme of $P$, and $\pi|_{W_s}:W_s\to U$ is an isomorphism with inverse $s$. Conversely, if $W\subseteq P$ is open and closed and $\pi|_W:W\to U$ is an isomorphism, $s=\iota_W\circ(\pi|_W)^{-1}$ is a section with $W_s=W$, and a section $s$ is recovered from $W_s$ as $\iota_{W_s}\circ(\pi|_{W_s})^{-1}$. So $s\mapsto W_s$ is a bijection from the sections of $\pi$ to the set of open and closed $W\subseteq P$ with $\pi|_W$ an isomorphism; the same holds for $\pi_0$, and $(W_s)\times_YY_0=W_{s_0}$. For every open and closed $W\subseteq P$, $\pi|_W=\pi\circ\iota_W$ is finite etale: $\iota_W$ is an open immersion, hence etale, and a closed immersion, hence finite, and compositions of finite, resp. etale, morphisms are finite, resp. etale.

source.place: Etale Morphisms, Proposition 024T and Schemes, Lemma 01KT (sections); the dictionary of the blueprint proof between Y-morphisms and clopen pieces of rank one

proof.text: *Clopen subsets correspond.* $P$ is finite over $U$, so $P\to S$ is proper (Step 1), with closed fibre $P_0$. Open and closed subsets of a scheme correspond to the idempotents of its ring of global sections. By [thm-weil-pbc-henselian-idempotent-lifting] applied to $P\to S$, $W\mapsto W_0=W\times_SS_0=W\cap P_0$ is a bijection from the open and closed subsets of $P$ to those of $P_0$. Applied to $U\to S$ (proper by Step 1), the injectivity says: an open and closed subset $T\subseteq U$ with $T\cap U_0=\emptyset$ is empty (it and $\emptyset$ have the same closed fibre).

source.place: ## Proof: the idempotent-lifting interface applied to the proper Z -> S

proof.text: *The degree-one condition descends.* Let $W\subseteq P$ be open and closed. If $\pi|_W$ is an isomorphism so is its base change $W_0\to U_0$. Conversely suppose $W_0\to U_0$ is an isomorphism. $\pi|_W$ is finite etale (Step 3), hence finite, flat and locally of finite presentation; let $r:U\to\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$ be its rank [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-rank-iso]. By (1) of that node $U_1=r^{-1}(1)$ is open and closed in $U$. By (2), for $u\in U_0$, $r(u)$ is the rank of the base change $W_0\to U_0$ at $u$, which is $1$ by (3) since $W_0\to U_0$ is an isomorphism; so $U_0\subseteq U_1$. Then $U\setminus U_1$ is open and closed and disjoint from $U_0$, hence empty by Step 4; so $r\equiv1$ and $\pi|_W$ is an isomorphism by (3). (The imported proof argued that the rank is determined on the image of $Y_0$ because $Y_0\to Y$ is surjective; $Y_0\to Y$ is a closed immersion and not surjective in general, and the step needs the fact of Step 4 that every nonempty clopen of $U$ meets $U_0$.)

source.place: ## Proof: rank of Z_e over Y is determined on the closed fibre

proof.text: *(a) Full faithfulness.* Composing Steps 2-5: $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(U,V)\cong\{$sections of $\pi\}\cong\{W\subseteq P$ clopen, $\pi|_W$ iso$\}\cong\{W_0\subseteq P_0$ clopen, $\pi_0|_{W_0}$ iso$\}\cong\{$sections of $\pi_0\}\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{Y_0}(U_0,V_0)$, the middle bijection being $W\mapsto W_0$ (Step 4, restricted by Step 5). Since $(s_\varphi)_0=s_{\varphi_0}$ and $(W_s)_0=W_{s_0}$, the composite is $\varphi\mapsto\varphi_0$. Hence $i^*$ is bijective on every Hom set: full and faithful, i.e. morphisms lift uniquely.

*(b) Essential surjectivity.* Every finite etale $Y_0$-scheme is isomorphic over $Y_0$ to $U_0$ for some $U\in\mathsf{FEt}(Y)$: this is [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-lifting-essential-surjectivity] (Stacks 0GS2, by algebraization in the Noetherian complete case, approximation in the G-ring case and a limit argument). It does not follow from idempotent lifting or from the degree-zero comparisons 0A0C/0A3S cited by the imported proof, which only give (a).

*(c) Equivalence.* A functor that is full, faithful and essentially surjective is an equivalence of categories (in Mathlib, `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsEquivalence` is the conjunction of `Faithful`, `Full` and `EssSurj`); apply this to $i^*$ with (a) and (b).

*(d) Group actions (formal consequence of (a) and (b)).* By (a), $i^*$ induces a bijection $\operatorname{End}_Y(Z)\to\operatorname{End}_{Y_0}(Z_0)$ compatible with composition and identities, hence a group isomorphism $\operatorname{Aut}_Y(Z)\to\operatorname{Aut}_{Y_0}(Z_0)$ ($\varphi$ is invertible iff $\varphi_0$ is, the inverse of $\varphi_0$ lifting to an inverse of $\varphi$ by faithfulness). An action of $G$ on $Z_0$ is a homomorphism $\rho_0:G\to\operatorname{Aut}_{Y_0}(Z_0)$; composing with the inverse group isomorphism gives the unique $\rho:G\to\operatorname{Aut}_Y(Z)$ with $\rho(g)_0=\rho_0(g)$. For $Z'\in\mathsf{FEt}(Y_0)$ with an action $\rho':G\to\operatorname{Aut}(Z')$, choose by (b) $Z$ and a $Y_0$-isomorphism $\alpha:Z_0\to Z'$, transport the action to $Z_0$ by $g\mapsto\alpha^{-1}\rho'(g)\alpha$ and lift it as before; $\alpha$ is then $G$-equivariant. Finiteness of $G$ is not needed.

blueprint_notes.label: status
blueprint_notes.text:
**Status.** The former proof invoked the torsion degree-zero comparison for
the map $H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)\to H^0(Z_0,\mathcal O_{Z_0})$ on structure
sheaves; that citation applies in neither reading, since the structure sheaf
is not torsion and the two sheaves are different objects. The needed statement
is the idempotent lifting interface
[thm-weil-pbc-henselian-idempotent-lifting], which the proof now cites. The
rest of the proof — properness of $Z$ over $S$, the dictionary between
$Y$-morphisms $Y\to Z$ and rank-one idempotents, the Hom-computation, and
uniqueness of the lifted group action — is proved here and depends on no
further input.
